title: TensorPlate Agent -> Serving Worker Control Contract (V01-E08-F05)
description:
Versioned local control messages between the V01-E08 agent and the V01-E07 serving worker.

Legacy operations (`prepare`, `capacity_check`, `warm`, `promote`, `active_status`, `unload`): v0.1.0 uses a typed in-process trait inside `tensorplate-agent` so the agent can target either (a) the real worker — by spawning it with a worker config that points at the staged bundle and polling its HTTP `/health` for readiness — or (b) a mock implementation for tests. They document the JSON shape of that trait and are never sent over the runtime control channel.

Runtime operations (`admission_fence`, `activate`, `retire`, `quota_assign`, `ledger_status`, `pressure_directive`) travel over the runtime control channel: a connected `AF_UNIX` stream socket pair the agent creates at spawn, whose other end the worker inherits as a descriptor, so there is no filesystem path and the peer is the agent by construction. A frame is one compact JSON document (no insignificant whitespace; keys in the order the golden frames `protocol/rust/tests/fixtures/worker_control_*.jsonl` use; strings in UTF-8 that escape only `\"`, `\\` and control characters, using `\b`, `\f`, `\n`, `\r` and `\t` where they apply and lowercase `\u00xx` otherwise; integers in plain decimal) followed by a single newline, at most 65536 bytes including the newline; a reader treats a longer line as a protocol error and closes the channel. A ledger reports at most 2048 sessions, so the largest `ok` `ledger_status` answer (2048 twenty-digit admission timestamps plus the envelope) stays under that limit; a writer keeps every frame within it, shortening an error message if it must. The agent sends one request per frame; the worker answers each with one response frame carrying the same `correlation_id`. Every runtime request names the `member` (deployment and generation) it is for and every runtime response names the member that answered, so a request for another generation is answered `member_mismatch`. `transaction_id` is the committing transaction for `admission_fence`, `activate` and `retire`, and the literal `runtime` for `quota_assign`, `ledger_status` and `pressure_directive`; on runtime frames both ids follow the shared `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}` policy.

Idempotency: each request on a channel has its own `correlation_id`. The agent repeats a request (for example after its deadline passed) with the same `correlation_id`, and only while it is the latest request the agent has sent on that channel. The worker keeps the `correlation_id` and outcome of the latest request it applied and answers a repeat of it with that outcome instead of applying it again, so a repeated `terminate_newest` cancels no further sessions and a repeated `retire` does not restart the drain its first application started. Any other `correlation_id` is a new request, so the worker keeps one such record per channel.

The agent is the only mutator of the worker's active deployment. The CLI never speaks this contract.

op.description: Operation. Legacy stages of the agent's prepare/warm/promote sequence: v0.1.0 collapses prepare+load into a single `prepare` call; `warm` is the readiness/health probe; `promote` switches the worker's active deployment after `warm` succeeds; `unload` releases the previous active when policy requires it. Runtime operations: `admission_fence` stops the member admitting new sessions and is acknowledged before the agent commits a set revision; `activate` opens admission under the member's assigned quota and answers with the quota in force; `retire` starts the member's retirement drain; `quota_assign` sets the member's session quota; `ledger_status` reports the member's session ledger; `pressure_directive` applies a memory pressure level.

drain_timeout_ms.description: How long a retiring member lets its existing sessions finish before they are cancelled.

timeout_ms.description: Bounded operation timeout enforced by the agent's worker client.

allOf.$comment: Runtime operations name their member and carry a correlation id; they never carry a candidate.

MemberRef.description: A resident-set member: one deployment at one generation.

PressureDirective.description: Memory pressure level the agent directs a member to apply. `normal` reports that no pressure applies and changes nothing. `shed_admission` stops admitting new sessions and drops droppable diagnostics. `terminate_newest` cancels the member's `count` newest admitted sessions. `resume` lifts `shed_admission`. Pressure levels never lift an `admission_fence` or undo a `retire`.

LedgerStatus.description: A member's session ledger. `reserved` sessions hold a quota reservation and are opening; `active` sessions are admitted and running; `closing` sessions are ending but hold their reservation until physical release. Together they never exceed `ceiling`, the member's session ceiling, which is at most 2048. `admission_monotonic_ns` lists, oldest first, the host monotonic-clock time at which each reserved or active session was admitted, so the agent can order the newest admitted sessions across members. Rules the decoder enforces beyond this schema: one timestamp per reserved or active session, in non-decreasing order (equal times are allowed), and reserved + active + closing <= ceiling.

MemberQuota.description: Session quota the agent assigned to the member: the concurrent session count (at most 2048, the most sessions one member's ledger reports) and the per-domain session quota bytes that back it. In qualification mode `session_count` is the operator's test count. A member that serves no logical sessions carries zero sessions and no domain bytes.

DomainQuotaBytes.description: Session quota bytes per budget domain. `shared_pool` (unified memory) never appears beside `guest_ram` or `device_vram` (discrete accelerator).

op.description: The runtime operation this response answers. Absent on legacy responses.

status.description: Outcome discriminator. `not_ready` is returned by `warm` while the candidate is still loading. `unsupported` maps to declared-but-unavailable backend or capability. `member_mismatch` answers a runtime request whose `member` is not the member this worker serves; the response's `member` names the one it does.

active_deployment_id.description: Deployment id currently serving traffic on the worker. Empty when no deployment has been promoted.

candidate_deployment_id.description: Deployment id of the most-recently-prepared candidate, if any.

ready.description: True when the worker reports the candidate (or current active, for `active_status`) as ready to serve.

allOf.$comment: A runtime response names its operation, echoes the request's transaction and correlation ids, and names the member that answered.
An ok activate or quota_assign answer publishes the quota now in force.
The legacy stage fields never appear on a runtime answer.
A runtime answer carries an error exactly when it failed.
